correctness.rationale: The five closure outputs are recalculated from exhaustive longest fixed-suffix checks. Direct occurrence searches establish six exact support sets: the first four are pairwise disjoint, while two additional factors each can be hit only through incompatible subintervals of the fourth support under a four-point hypothesis. Hence gamma>=5. The five witness positions have unmarked runs at most nine, and exact exhaustive comparison of the factor sets for lengths 1 through 9 proves they attract every shorter factor; all longer occurrences automatically meet the set, hence gamma<=5. No infinite inference from finite sampling is needed.

evidence: Dvořáková–Hendrychová prove two- and three-position attractors in defined subfamilies and leave the four-bound universally conjectural.
Kutsukake et al. show the completed finite Thue–Morse words have minimum four.
Schaeffer–Shallit provide automatic-sequence prefix results, not a universal bound for all closure directives.
Dolce treats factors of a fixed Thue–Morse word and proves a sharp upper bound of five there.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The scopes in these results are limited to particular languages or directive subfamilies. They neither force all generalized pseudostandard prefixes to have at most four positions nor provide this constructed counterexample. Dolce establishes the number five for some factors of a different specified language, not the counterexample status of the displayed closure-prefix word.

originality.rationale: The main relevant 2023/2024 full text expressly conjectures an upper bound of four for exactly this closure-defined class. The verified word with gamma=5 provides a direct counterexample. The published Thue–Morse and special Rote/pseudostandard subclass theorems are strictly narrower and do not imply the exhibited counterexample. A semantic and exact-term search of relevant public literature did not surface an earlier equivalent; unindexed priority remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased earlier counterexample may exist.
The theorem demonstrates existence but does not identify the shortest possible counterexample, nor determine a general maximum attractor size.

value.rationale: An explicit construction with a short human-inspectable six-factor obstruction disproves a published universal conjecture, a motivated and mathematically meaningful boundary for string attractors of generalized pseudostandard words. The exact five-set witness is independently reproducible. This has significance beyond computing an arbitrary small numerical invariant.
